newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends sharply higher after EU news.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends sharply higher after EU news.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed sharply higher after buyers jumped into the market assuming U.S. wheat prices will increase after the European Commission suspended exports of subsidized wheat, traders said.
Non-subsidized EU wheat sales would be allowed to continue, but EU officials said Thursday subsidized sales, which has been the bulk of the volume, would be discontinued until July.

"If exports out of Europe are suspended, it would most definitely affect our U.S. wheat exports," said a senior U.S. wheat export trader. "There is no alternative but the U.S. when you are talking July, August, and September (positions)."
Gains in KCBT wheat accelerated when July rose through $4.55 per bushel, the previous weekly high, which prompted active shortcovering by commission houses and commodity funds, traders said.
The EU news intensifies concerns about about supplies, particularly as agronomists assess the damage two-days of freezing temperatures did to hard red winter wheat in Kansas, Oklahoma and Texas.
KCBT wheat closed 22-3/4 to four cents higher, with May up 17 at $4.82 and July up the most at $4.62-3/4 per bushel.
Estimated volume for Thursday was 56.755 million bushels.
